_verified: 2026-09-13: tier ids, output caps and context windows read from the Models API (models.retrieve) and the output cap confirmed by an over-limit 400. Both tiers pinged clean. Context window is reported by the provider, not assumed.

light._note: One API key serves both tiers — Anthropic does not split keys by tier, unlike the two Gemini keys that isolate Flash volume from Pro quota. thinking_levels maps onto output_config.effort; the provider also accepts xhigh and max, which QueryHints has no vocabulary for. 'minimal' is absent because there is no such effort level.

heavy._fallback_note: Both are GA aliases rather than dated snapshots, so a retirement is unlikely; Sonnet 5 is named as the substitute because it shares the same request surface and caps.

request_constraints._note: Rejected parameters, verified against the Models API capability block. Sending any of these is a 400, so no client may pass them for this provider.

application/pdf._verified: 2026-09-24, both tiers (claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-5), inline base64 document block. tokens_per_page MEASURED: (document-call input_tokens - same prompt as text) / pages on the 3-page probe PDF; identical on both tiers, and 60% above the 1500 placeholder it replaces. Page cost does not vary with media_resolution here, so the per-resolution block is filled uniformly. max_pages is the LARGEST COUNT VERIFIED, not a refusal: 101 and 250 pages were accepted and counted correctly; the 1,000,000-token context window binds at ~415 pages. max_size_mb is MEASURED against the decoded file: the documented 32 MB limit covers the request including base64, so a 20 MB PDF (27 MB encoded) was accepted and a 25 MB PDF (33 MB encoded) was refused twice. The refusal arrives as a dropped connection, which the client classifies as transient, so this guard must stop an oversized document before it is sent.
application/pdf._note: Inline only, never the Files API: an upload is retained provider-side until deleted. No gs_uri path: this provider cannot read a GCS URI, so the dispatcher reads the bytes first (no remote_uri_gs capability).

output_budget._note: Thinking tokens are output tokens and come out of max_tokens, as on Gemini — but budget_tokens was removed on the 5 family, so depth is set by output_config.effort and the spend is adaptive rather than capped. These reserves are what to hold back when sizing how much content one call may emit; max_tokens is a ceiling, not a charge, so reserving generously costs nothing unless spent.
